bug_report_content:
id: 416
status: Fixed
summary: Codepoint U+007f appears raw in output
labels: ['Type-Defect', 'Priority-Medium']
stars: 1
commentCount: 7
Comment 0 (2011-04-11): What steps will reproduce the problem? 1. Open http://closure-compiler.appspot.com/home in your browser 2. Enter the source code: alert('\x7f') 3. Hit the "Compile" button. What is the expected output? alert("\x7f") What do you see instead? alert(""); What version of the product are you using? On what operating system? The version live on 11 April 2011. Please provide any additional information below. Codepoint U+007f is a delete control character and is the only non-printable ASCII codepoint that is not <= U+0020. http://www.fileformat.info/info/unicode/char/7f/index.htm It should probably not appear raw in emitted source code because, it can confuse encoders.
Comment 2 (2011-04-12): It go to the code, but is non-visible. alert('\x7f'); // Result will have 11 bytes alert(''); // Result will have 10 bytes
Comment 3 (2011-04-12): Yes. It is there. U+007f is not a printable character, so it should probably not appear in the output the way U+001f does not appear raw in the output.
Comment 4 (2011-04-15): I haven't commonly seen the \x## encoding. Is it consistently support by all browsers (by that I mean IE6-9, Chrome 10+, FF3+, Opera 11+, Safari 5)
Comment 5 (2011-04-15): Closure compiler recognizes them just fine but does not seem to emit them. The input alert('\u007f') produces the same compiler output as alert('\x7f') Section 7.8.4 of the EcmaScript 3 spec defines EscapeSequence thus EscapeSequence :: CharacterEscapeSequence OctalEscapeSequence HexEscapeSequence UnicodeEscapeSequence ... HexEscapeSequence :: x HexDigit HexDigit EcmaScript 3 disallows OctalEscapeSequence (but allows it as an optional extension in an annex) but allows \0 not followed by [0-9].
Comment 6 (2011-04-16): This issue was closed by revision r1014.
